text:
incident-bot: Paging on-call SRE (olivia_sre). Suspicious traffic: repeated /auth/callback POSTs with valid session tokens from 3 IPs that mirror legitimate client behavior. Rate spike + 401 churn. Investigate.

olivia_sre: ack. joining. grabbing logs and looking at edge traces.
miguel_devops: seeing pattern from aws-030-185-xx-yy (ranges) via mirror-proxy-prod. Sampling shows payloads identical to valid requests but different X-Forwarded-For.
ryan_backend: if they're replaying sessions through the mirror proxy, they may be scraping tokens cached in some intermediate. Code change deployed last week to mirror-proxy for debug sampling — can we disable sampling quickly?
miguel_devops: yes. disabling mirror sampling now: `curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/v1/config/mirror-proxy -d '{"sampling":0}'` -> response 202.
olivia_sre: sampling disabled at edge (t+2m). traffic spike dropping ~70% already. continuing to tail logs.
jamie_sec: quick question — any evidence of token exfil from logs or S3? we need triage on possible PII.
miguel_devops: staging-forwarder job has deliveries to a customer S3 bucket, but current events show requests to prod endpoints, not staging. no obvious S3 PUTs matching those request ids.
ryan_backend: auth-service logs show repeated token validation calls for those sessions — some succeed, some 401. pattern suggests a client is replaying recent bearer tokens. We should invalidate recent refresh tokens for affected sessions.
olivia_sre: agreed. mitigation checklist proposal: 1) block offending IP ranges at WAF; 2) disable mirror-proxy sampling (done); 3) kick sessions via auth-service /sessions/invalidate for tokens with last-used <48h from those client IDs; 4) audit staging forwarder config; 5) plan key/service-account rotation if we find exfil.
lina_support: any customer impact yet? Do we need to prepare outbound comms?\olj: (typo)
jamie_sec: preliminary customer impact: no confirmed account takeovers. authentication noise (increased 401s) may have affected a small percentage of users with long-lived sessions. continue monitoring.
ryan_backend: running targeted invalidation now for client_ids seen in the logs: `POST /internal/auth/invalidate` body: `{"client_ids": ["web-abc","mobile-xyz"], "since": "-48h"}` -> job queued.
miguel_devops: WAF rules pushed to block 3 IP ranges and set challenge for fingerprints. `aws wafv2 update-web-acl` executed t+8m.
olivia_sre: live metrics: auth 5xx stable, 401 churn down 60%. sessions invalidation job started t+10m, estimated completion t+13m.
jamie_sec: while we wait run a quick grep for sensitive headers in the last 24h logs and check S3 access logs for staging-forwarder keys. if anything shows PUTs with matching request ids, escalate.
miguel_devops: grep in progress — scanning S3 access logs + forwarder logs.
ryan_backend: note: we added an ephemeral revoke endpoint yesterday for bulk session invalidation; it uses service-account `svc-auth-rotator`. If that account keys are in any place that could be leaked, rotate them after this immediate mitigation.
jamie_sec: start key rotation prep now. generate new key for svc-auth-rotator, stage it to auth-rotator pod, then rotate env var via k8s secret and restart pods. hold final rotation until we confirm no exfil evidence.
olivia_sre: agreed. action owner mapping: miguel -> block + log scan; ryan -> session invalidation + monitoring; jamie -> key rotation plan; olivia -> incident lead + customer impact. lina -> prepare support playbook.
lina_support: drafting playbook: short note to affected customers if we confirm token compromise; for now outbound guidance: "We detected suspicious attempts; we've invalidated sessions and are monitoring. No confirmed exposure."
incident-bot: Incident declared: SEV-2 "mirror-proxy token replay". Page 1 on-call list.
ryan_backend: session invalidation job completed t+14m. logs show ~2.1k sessions invalidated tied to the suspicious client_ids.
miguel_devops: S3 scan complete: no matching PUTs or suspicious access patterns from the mirror-proxy service role in the last 72h. forwarder config had an extra debug webhook but it was disabled last month.
jamie_sec: still proceed with svc-auth-rotator key rotation as precaution — generating new key now and will roll to staging then prod. ETA 45m.
olivia_sre: can we add a short-term rule to auth-service that rejects tokens presented via mirror-proxy UA/fingerprint? we can fast-fail those while we continue investigation.
ryan_backend: implemented `revocation-list` check in auth-service and added fingerprint block for `mirror-proxy/1.2-debug` header. deployed to canary (10%).
olivia_sre: canary looks good. roll to 100% in 5m.
lina_support: support playbook updated with steps and canned responses. prepping internal CS notes.
jamie_sec: I've started the key creation. will update when new key is active.
miguel_devops: WAF blocks holding. spike reduced to baseline plus noise.
olivia_sre: current verdict: likely opportunistic token replay via mirror-proxy debug sampling. No confirmed data exfil to external buckets. Mitigations: sampling disabled, blocked IPs, invalidated ~2.1k sessions, added fingerprint blocks, key rotation in progress as precaution.
incident-bot: Handoff: on-call shift change in 6h. olivia_sre will lead postmortem. Please add notes to the incident tracker: `INC-2024-042`.
ryan_backend: will gather logs and dashboards for postmortem (latency, auth error rates, token churn) and link to tracker.
jamie_sec: will prepare timeline and rotation audit.
miguel_devops: will include infra diffs showing mirror-proxy sampling toggle and WAF rule IDs.
lina_support: will include customer queries and any tickets opened.
olivia_sre: next steps: monitor for 24h, complete key rotation, finalize external comms only if we find confirmed token export. otherwise close with mitigation summary.
incident-bot: Incident status -> Mitigated (actions applied). Update incident tracker when you close. :white_check_mark:
